title: Why marine climate refugia matters for safeguarding the world’s oceans
content:
KEY TAKEAWAYS

  • Marine climate refugia are areas where relatively stable environmental conditions help species and ecosystems withstand climate change.

    • Marine climate refugia are areas where relatively stable environmental conditions help species and ecosystems withstand climate change.

  • They are identified through three approaches: low exposure, ecological resilience and habitat suitability.

    • They are identified through three approaches: low exposure, ecological resilience and habitat suitability.

  • Further research and proactive management are urgently needed to strengthen ocean resilience as marine climate refugia face growing threats.

    • Further research and proactive management are urgently needed to strengthen ocean resilience as marine climate refugia face growing threats.

    The ocean is changing rapidly. Warming, acidification, oxygen loss, sea-level rise, and the intensification of extreme events are transforming marine ecosystems, leading to species shifts and mass mortality events. However, these impacts are not distributed evenly. There are areas that buffer these effects and act as true “marine climate refugia”.
snippet:
KEY TAKEAWAYS

Marine climate refugia are areas where relatively stable environmental conditions help species and ecosystems withstand climate change.
creator: Marina Sanz-Martín, AXA Fellow, Fonds Axa pour le progrès humain; Instituto Español de Oceanografía (IEO - CSIC)

title: Policing protests: how France’s student movement echoes the political crisis in Kanaky-New Caledonia
content:
KEY TAKEAWAYS

  • The French authorities have responded to protests with arrests, police violence, curfews and restrictions rather than dialogue in hexagonal France and in its overseas territories.

    • The French authorities have responded to protests with arrests, police violence, curfews and restrictions rather than dialogue in hexagonal France and in its overseas territories.

  • Young people are protesting against key issues such as poor means for education, unemployment, rising inequalities equating to a lack of opportunities. These problems are particularly severe in Kanaky-New Caledonia, where socio-economic inequalities are also linked to ethnic discrimination.

    • Young people are protesting against key issues such as poor means for education, unemployment, rising inequalities equating to a lack of opportunities. These problems are particularly severe in Kanaky-New Caledonia, where socio-economic inequalities are also linked to ethnic discrimination.

  • Younger generations feel ignored by political leaders, while older voters have greater influence over elections and political decisions. In both France and Kanaky-New Caledonia, protesters feel their voices and demands are not being heard.

title: Can AI feel safer than human advice for consumers who face discrimination?
content:
KEY TAKEAWAYS

  • A study highlights that consumers who have experienced discrimination are more likely to turn to AI-based recommendations rather than human advice.

    • A study highlights that consumers who have experienced discrimination are more likely to turn to AI-based recommendations rather than human advice.

  • The fear of being judged or feeling embarrassed can lead people to use AI.

    • The fear of being judged or feeling embarrassed can lead people to use AI.

  • If AI systems are themselves biased, they risk exacerbating the very discrimination that consumers were trying to escape.

    • If AI systems are themselves biased, they risk exacerbating the very discrimination that consumers were trying to escape.

    What should you cook for dinner on a budget of 20 euros when you have a guest with a gluten intolerance? A shopper might ask a shop assistant for advice or consult, for example, Hopla, the AI-powered shopping assistant launched by French supermarket chain Carrefour. Behind this very ordinary everyday choice lies a broader question: when faced with a recommendation, who do we trust more? A human being or an AI?

KEY TAKEAWAYS

title: Five ways to beat dating algorithms at their own game
content:
KEY TAKEAWAYS

  • Decide what you want before you start swiping. An app can suggest people to meet, but it cannot decide what kind of relationship matters to you.

    • Decide what you want before you start swiping. An app can suggest people to meet, but it cannot decide what kind of relationship matters to you.

  • Set limits on your time and attention. More profiles and more matches do not necessarily bring you closer to a meaningful connection.

title: What is umami?
content:
Characterised at the beginning of the 20th century in Japan, umami literally means “delicious taste” or “tasty taste”. Umami flavour was accepted as one of the five basic tastes at the beginning of the 2000s, on the basis of its detection by the taste receptors present within the patches of tissue or papillae on our tongue. Umami’s distinctive, savoury flavour is mainly produced by certain amino acids that make up proteins, including glutamic acid or its salt form, glutamate (sodium).

Umami has a unique characteristic: a phenomenon of synergy. This means that the flavour of glutamate is drastically increased by certain compounds found in certain foods or ingredients such as bonito – a cousin of tuna – dried (katsuobushi) or yeast extracts.

Although many molecules can produce the umami taste, it is one of the most little known and difficult sensations to describe, mainly because of the rarity of compounds that possess a pure umami taste.

title: Are insects really ‘poor people’s food’?
content:
KEY TAKEAWAYS

  • Eating insects is often perceived only as a last resort in case of famine or extreme poverty.

    • Eating insects is often perceived only as a last resort in case of famine or extreme poverty.

  • Yet, in the countries where they are usually eaten, insects are often considered a rare delicacy, even a luxury, because the prized species are difficult to track down.

    • Yet, in the countries where they are usually eaten, insects are often considered a rare delicacy, even a luxury, because the prized species are difficult to track down.

  • In some cases, consuming insects also helps to control the proliferation of crop pests.

    • In some cases, consuming insects also helps to control the proliferation of crop pests.

    Do people eat insects when there is nothing else to eat? Are insects really “food for the poor” or famine food?

    In the West, insects weren’t considered as food but as vermin, crop pests, vectors of disease or sources of unpleasant bites, while other societies learned to live with them, as ethnobiologist Darrell Posey had already noted in 1978 about Amazonian people.

title: Why the student protests in France and the government’s response are unprecedented and unpredictable
content:
KEY TAKEAWAYS

  • The mass nationwide movement led by high school students, joined by their parents, teachers and trade unions, brought together 450,000 protesters on October 6 (250,000, according to the French government).

    • The mass nationwide movement led by high school students, joined by their parents, teachers and trade unions, brought together 450,000 protesters on October 6 (250,000, according to the French government).

  • French lycée students’ demands for better resources and conditions in schools are recurrent, but what’s new is the global context, the nature of the movement and where it started out: in France’s working suburbs.

  • The government’s response, which first opted for confrontation before favouring negotiations, has created an explosive situation whose outcome is very uncertain.
